claims.text: UN News (citing OHCHR/UN High Commissioner Volker Turk), reporting on Yemen: 'at least 17 civilians were killed in Houthi attacks on government-controlled areas since August 6, 2026.' Specific incidents cited: a missile strike on the Jaw al-Naseem displacement camp in Ma'rib (7 August) injuring six civilians including a child; missile and drone attacks on Al-Mokha port in Ta'izz Governorate (9 August) killing three port workers and injuring four others; and an attack on a cargo ship in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (11 August) killing four crew members (three Pakistani nationals, one Indonesian) with additional injuries. Turk said: 'I call on all parties to de-escalate tensions and spare the Yemeni people from further misery' and 'These attacks must end immediately.'

UN News (18 September 2026), 'Yemen's humanitarian crisis growing by the hour amid spike in displacement': the International Organization for Migration reports 'at least 112,000 people' have been displaced inside Yemen over the last two weeks, mainly along the west coast and in Aden, Hudaydah, Abyan and Taiz governorates, on top of the 4.8 million Yemenis already displaced by years of prior conflict; more than 3,000 people have now crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Djibouti, arriving on overcrowded boats with very limited food and water. IOM Chief of Mission Abdusattor Esoev said, 'Our resources are very, very, very limited and our stocks will be depleted very soon.' OHCHR spokesperson Shabia Mantoo said Yemeni civilians 'are already bearing the consequences of renewed full-scale hostilities,' and the article notes 73 UN personnel remain arbitrarily detained by Houthi authorities, some since 2021, with only 60 of Yemen's more than 5,000 health service delivery units fully functioning.

OCHA Djibouti's 'New Arrivals from Yemen Flash Update No. 1' (15 September 2026): 'More than 2,500 people fleeing conflict in Yemen have arrived on Djibouti's northern coast as of 14 September.' This is confirmed and updated by UN News's 18 September report (already on file), which puts the figure at 'more than 3,000 people' who have crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Djibouti. WHO's Yemen Conflict Escalation Situation Report #3 (13 September, reporting period 6-12 September, posted 15 September) remains the latest in its numbered series, confirming cumulative casualties 'rose from 1,137 ... to 2,883 as of 12 September: 2,379 injuries and 504 deaths' and that DFA (Houthi) forces control the entire west coast except Midi district, following their 10-11 September seizure of the Bab el-Mandeb coast including Mocha, Dhubab and Perim (Mayyun) Island.

UN News (22 September 2026), 'Displacement on the rise in Yemen as fighting continues': UNHCR spokesperson Babar Baloch said fighting in Yemen 'is expanding across multiple front lines, triggering a rapidly growing displacement crisis and driving more than 130,000 people to flee their homes since the beginning of September,' with Taiz governorate accounting for more than 60 percent of overall displacement; more than 3,000 people have arrived in Djibouti, with arrivals projected to exceed 10,000 by mid-October, and over 22 million people -- more than half of Yemen's population -- are estimated to need humanitarian assistance.

UN Security Council Press Statement SC/16458, 'Security Council Press Statement on Escalation in Yemen, Attacks against Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,' issued 18 September 2026 by Council President Jerome Bonnafont (France) and confirmed on the Council's Yemen press-release listing (press.un.org/en/yemen): Council members condemned continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, including attacks affecting civilian and energy infrastructure that injured civilians, affirmed Saudi Arabia's right to self-defense, and demanded the Houthis immediately cease their military escalation.

UN News (29 September 2026), citing WHO and Aden health authorities: 'since 6 August, the renewed clashes in southwest Yemen have left more than 4,481 casualties including 830 deaths,' and 'more than 180,000 people have now been uprooted by the fighting.' The article also reports that only about 60 percent of health facilities are fully functional, with nine health facilities damaged, put out of service or directly attacked, mostly near Taiz, Lahj and Hudaydah, and that emergency obstetric care has been suspended at two hospitals as staff are redirected to trauma care.

The same UN News article (29 September 2026) reports that Yemen's conflict escalation has fueled rising disease risk: approximately 7,800 suspected cholera cases with 22 deaths reported in 2026, more than 22,000 identified measles cases, and dengue linked to 37 deaths. It also reports that WHO's Aden warehouse has several lifesaving supply lines, including trauma kits and essential medicines, at zero stock, with the organisation having so far secured only a small fraction of the funding it needs for its emergency response.

UN News (25 September 2026), 'Yemen violence deepens concerns over child hunger crisis': UNICEF has verified that at least 15 children have been killed and 14 injured in Yemen since 3 September, with three more reported missing; about 71,000 children are among nearly 130,000 people displaced over the past three weeks, with most displacement in Taiz governorate. Of nearly 2,900 children screened in areas with safe humanitarian access, more than one in four was acutely malnourished, including about 200 with severe acute malnutrition, compounding a pre-existing caseload of more than 2.2 million Yemeni children under five projected to be acutely malnourished in 2026.

UNHCR's 'Yemen Situation: External Update #2' (dated 28 September 2026, published 1 October 2026) records approximately 142,000 people (more than 23,660 households) newly displaced across seven governorates between 1 August and 27 September 2026 (excluding Al Hodeidah, where access was unavailable); Taiz hosts 56% of this group, Lahj 26% and Aden 8%. The same update records almost 3,793 refugees who have crossed by sea to Djibouti and about 150 who reached Somaliland/Puntland, and notes more than 63,000 refugees and asylum-seekers already in Yemen are also affected; UNHCR's $193.6 million 2026 Yemen funding requirement is only 18% funded.

UN News (7 October 2026), 'Critical funding gap threatens health response in Yemen': citing Yemeni health authorities, 'as of 2 October, there were 959 reported deaths and 4,207 injuries across 10 governorates'; the International Organization for Migration reports 'more than 200,000 people have been displaced,' with 'close to 3,800' having fled to Djibouti across the Red Sea; the World Health Organization said that 'of the nearly 198,000 people who have been uprooted,' less than one percent had received health services as of the previous week, and that its immediate funding requirement has increased from $9 million to $31 million, with an additional $700,000 needed to support refugees in Djibouti.

UN News (13 October 2026), 'Yemen: Houthi siege, cholera outbreak and aid cuts put civilians in the crosshairs': citing WHO, 'the country has reported 8,034 suspected cholera cases and 27 deaths this year' and 'more than 22,800 suspected [measles] cases and 128 deaths reported this year'; 'since August, 200,000 people have been displaced'; the Houthis 'tightened their blockade at the start of this month' by taking 'control of the last main road between Taiz and other government-held areas'; WHO's 90-day emergency response 'needs $31 million and has received just $4.3 million, less than 14 per cent of the total.' The same coverage reports that Saudi authorities said a separate Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300.

UN News, Security Council coverage (13 August 2026): UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg briefed the Security Council warning Yemen 'faces a more serious risk of return to large-scale conflict than at any point since' the 2022 UN-mediated truce, citing intensifying military activity along the frontline and pressure on regional trade and energy flows. UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher told the Council more than half of Yemen's population faces acute food insecurity, and with the humanitarian appeal only 20 percent funded, 'rations are cut, clinics close and protection services disappear'; both officials called for the immediate release of 73 UN colleagues still arbitrarily detained by the Houthis.

IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix 'Yemen - Displacement Caused by Escalation in the West Coast - Update #14' (period covered 1 August-13 October 2026) records 227,683 people (about 37,946 households) displaced since 1 August 2026, and 228,739 people (38,122 households) cumulatively since the West Coast escalation began in June 2026. Ta'iz governorate accounts for the largest share, 121,104 people (53%), followed by Lahj (51,984, 23%), Aden (27,348, 12%), Abyan (11,838, 5%) and Al Hodeidah (8,244, 4%), with smaller numbers in Hadramawt, Shabwah, Ma'rib, Al Maharah and Ad Dali'.

WHO's Conflict Escalation in Yemen Situation Report #8 (reporting period 12-19 October 2026, issued 20 October 2026) records the MoPHP Health Emergency Operations Centre's cumulative casualty register at 8,513 (6,939 injured, 1,574 deaths) by 19 October, an increase of 1,340 (1,048 injured, 292 deaths) since Sitrep #7's 7,173 cumulative total at 11 October, with a new front having opened in Shabwah governorate (216 casualties, 51 deaths in two days) alongside continued fighting in Marib, Lahj, Taiz and Al-Dhale'e. IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix recorded 42,764 households (256,591 people) displaced as of 19 October, up about 28% from 201,217 on 7 October, with Taiz both the largest origin and destination governorate. Access into Taiz city remains the most critical gap: the main Haygat Al-Abd road is cut, 42 health facilities report acute shortages, and the Joint Medical Emergency Committee estimates US$624,900 is needed to keep five public hospitals running for three months. Suspected cholera cases across the five most-affected governorates declined to 562 in epidemiological week 41, down from a peak of 639 in week 40.

IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix 'Yemen - Displacement Caused by Escalation in Western Yemen - Update #15' (published 21 October 2026) recorded an increase of 8,682 individual IDPs on 20 October alone, bringing displacement between 1 August and 20 October 2026 to about 258,751 people (43,119 households), and the cumulative total since the escalation began in June 2026 to 259,807 people (43,295 households). Ta'iz governorate remains the largest share at 124,092 people (48%), followed by Lahj (65,238, 25%) and Aden (38,400, 15%).

IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix 'Yemen - Displacement Caused by Escalation in Western Yemen - Update Dataset (25 October 2026)' records 276,301 internally displaced persons (46,044 households) tracked since the escalation began in June 2026, as of 24 October 2026, up from 259,807 as of 20 October; of this, 275,245 individuals (45,868 households) were displaced between 1 August and 24 October 2026. Ta'iz governorate remains the largest share at 126,156 individuals (46%), followed by Lahj (68,832, 25%) and Aden (47,400, 17%).

IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix 'Yemen - Displacement Caused by Escalation in Western Yemen - Update Dataset (28 October 2026)' records 287,767 internally displaced persons (47,955 households) tracked since the escalation began in June 2026, as of 27 October 2026, up from 276,301 as of 24 October (an increase of 12,522 individuals recorded on 27 October alone compared with the prior day's report); of this, about 286,711 individuals (47,779 households) were displaced between 1 August and 27 October 2026. Ta'iz governorate remains the largest share at 128,484 individuals (45%), followed by Lahj (71,100, 25%) and Aden (53,016, 18%).

UN News (29 October 2026), 'World News in Brief': citing WHO, the organization delivered trauma and emergency-surgery kits to hospitals in Taiz city, which remains almost entirely surrounded by Houthi forces; movement restrictions have halted community midwife services and there are acute shortages of medicines, fuel and water. In Marib governorate, WHO said primary healthcare is on the 'verge of collapse' because of funding cuts: 'Only six out of 31 mobile medical teams are still operational,' and 15 health facilities have stopped functioning.

UN News (10 September 2026), reporting on the Security Council briefing on Yemen: fighting since 3 September has newly displaced more than 11,400 households, with humanitarian partners providing emergency assistance to over 2,700 of the displaced households; on the morning of 10 September, Houthi forces seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha (about 75km from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait), and eight UN vehicles were seized from a humanitarian hub in the same operation. UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg told the Council: 'The risk has now turned into a harsh reality,' and that the question facing the international community is no longer whether war in Yemen will resume, but how to respond to 'a new, more dangerous phase.'

WHO's Conflict Escalation in Yemen Situation Report #9 (reporting period 20-25 October 2026, issued 28 October 2026) records the MoPHP Health Emergency Operations Centre's cumulative casualty register at 9,072 (7,395 injured, 1,677 deaths) by 25 October, an increase of 559 (456 injured, 103 deaths) since Sitrep #8's 8,513 at 19 October. Marib was the most lethal front, recording 45 deaths among 143 casualties (31%), more than Taiz (34 of 237) or Lahj (21 of 158); on 22 and 23 October, deaths in Marib outnumbered injuries. The Shabwah Health Office revised the toll from the 19 October missile strike on Al-Alam Camp near Ataq upward to 235 casualties (69 deaths, 166 injured), with 21 critical patients transferred to Mukalla. IOM's DTM recorded 276,301 people displaced (46,044 households) as of 24 October, with the pace of new displacement slowing sharply after mid-October. Suspected cholera cases across the five most-affected governorates declined to 447 in week 42, down from a peak of 639 in week 40, though 3 confirmed cases and 1 death in Marib point to possible spread beyond the southern belt; Marib's primary healthcare network has weakened further, with only 6 of 31 mobile medical teams still operating (down from 31 in 2025) and 15 facilities non-functional.

IOM's DTM 'Yemen - Displacement Caused by Escalation in Western Yemen - Update Dataset (31 October 2026)' records cumulative displacement since the escalation began in June 2026 at 300,391 individuals (50,059 households) as of 31 October 2026, up from 287,767 as of 27 October. Displacement for 1 August-31 October totals approximately 299,335 individuals (49,883 households); Ta'iz remains the largest governorate with 133,800 (45%), followed by Lahj with 73,110 (24%) and Aden with 56,934 (19%).

UN Security Council meeting coverage, SC/16449, 10219th Meeting (10 September 2026): the Houthis 'have gained control of the port city of Mokha, which lies roughly 75 kilometres from the Bab el-Mandeb strait,' giving them a direct presence on the approaches to one of the world's most vital shipping straits; Special Envoy Hans Grundberg told the Council that the period of relative calm prevailing in the country over the last four years -- since the 2022 UN-mediated truce -- has ended. Latvia's representative told the Council that 'in just 72 hours since the escalation of hostilities on 3 September, approximately 18,500 people have reportedly been displaced along Yemen's west coast, with displacement continuing to rise by the hour.'

UN News (11 September 2026): the International Organization for Migration reports 'at least 46,000 people have been displaced' since renewed fighting began in Yemen's West Coast and Taiz governorates, a figure IOM said is 'alarmingly rising by the hour,' with new arrivals reported in Lahj and Aden and movement northward toward Ibb. OCHA separately reported 'at least 14 civilians, including two children, had been killed or wounded since the beginning of the month.' Houthi fighters seized control of the strategically important Red Sea port city of Mokha earlier in the week, prompting mass departures, and pro-government forces reportedly withdrew Friday (11 September) from an island base in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, with militants pledging to continue targeting Saudi shipping in the area.
UN News (11 September 2026) reports that the World Health Organization 'recorded 67 deaths and 288 injuries between 6-24 August' in seven Yemeni governorates.

UN News (14 September 2026), citing OCHA and OHCHR: 'At least 18,000 households -- or 125,000 people -- have been displaced since the start of the month' by hostilities in Yemen, with 80,000 people displaced 'by escalating fighting in Yemen in recent days'; separately, 'Between 1 September and Monday, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, has verified 40 civilian casualties -- eight people killed and 32 others injured,' with women and children accounting for half of those killed and more than half of those injured. The article also reports that Houthi fighters 'have seized multiple islands in the Red Sea and a crucial Yemeni port city, giving them greater control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait,' in addition to the earlier seizure of eight UN vehicles from a key aid hub.

UN News (15 September 2026), reporting on an emergency Security Council session on Yemen: the World Health Organization reports '2,883 casualties since 6 August,' and the International Organization for Migration stated '93,864 have been newly displaced' since fighting intensified earlier this month; WHO's latest situation report also recorded 'seven health facilities and assets damaged, out of service or directly hit in 10 days.' The Houthis seized several further Red Sea islands in the preceding week, and UNHCR said escalating hostilities along Yemen's west coast have forced thousands more to seek safety across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in Djibouti.

UN News (15 September 2026), 'Escalating conflict drives new displacement in Yemen': 'Over 2,400 people fled to Djibouti within four days, with more than 60% being women, children, and elderly individuals'; continued insecurity could disrupt humanitarian and commercial shipping serving Yemen, Sudan and other emergencies, with potential diversions via the Cape of Good Hope adding 25-30 days to shipping times. UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher released US$9 million from the Central Emergency Response Fund for urgent assistance to displaced families and receiving communities. Nearly half of Yemen's 41 million people need aid as acute hunger continues to grow.

description: Houthi (DFA) forces have encircled Taiz and expanded fighting into Marib and Shabwah governorates amid Yemen's conflict escalation that began in June 2026. WHO's Situation Report #9 (20-25 October) puts cumulative casualties at 9,072 (7,395 injured, 1,677 deaths), up 559 in six days, with Marib now the most lethal front and a missile strike on Shabwah's Al-Alam Camp revised upward to 235 casualties. IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix records 300,391 people displaced since the escalation began, as of 31 October. Taiz city's hospital system remains near breaking point, with its main supply road cut and WHO delivering trauma kits there on 24 October; in Marib, only 6 of 31 mobile medical teams remain operational amid funding cuts. Suspected cholera cases have declined to 447 in week 42 across the worst-affected governorates, down from a week-40 peak of 639, though new cases in Marib suggest possible spread.

impact.summary: WHO's Conflict Escalation Situation Report #9 (28 October 2026, period 20-25 October) puts cumulative casualties at 9,072 (7,395 injured, 1,677 deaths) as of 25 October, up 559 in six days; Marib is now the most lethal front, recording 45 deaths among 143 casualties, and the Shabwah Health Office revised the toll from the 19 October Al-Alam Camp missile strike upward to 235 casualties (69 deaths). IOM's DTM dataset (31 October) puts cumulative displacement since the escalation began in June 2026 at 300,391 people (50,059 households) as of 31 October, up from 287,767 on 27 October; Ta'iz remains the largest governorate (45%), followed by Lahj (24%) and Aden (19%). Taiz city's hospital system is near breaking point -- its main supply road is cut, and WHO delivered trauma kits to three hospitals and a health centre there on 24 October -- while in Marib, funding cuts have left only 6 of 31 mobile medical teams operational and 15 facilities shut. Suspected cholera cases have declined to 447 in week 42 across the five most-affected governorates, down from a peak of 639 in week 40, though 3 confirmed cases and 1 death in Marib point to possible spread beyond the southern belt.

location.region: Ta'izz Governorate (Mocha, Al-Mokha) and Yemen's West Coast; attacks also in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and against Saudi Arabia

event.scale: DFA (Houthi) forces control the entire west coast except Midi district and have largely encircled Taiz, with Marib now the most lethal front; WHO records 9,072 cumulative casualties (1,677 deaths) as of 25 October and IOM 287,767 displaced as of 27 October 2026

name: Yemen Conflict Escalation

updates.text: IOM's DTM update dataset (31 October) recorded displacement since the escalation began in June 2026 rising to 300,391 people (50,059 households) as of 31 October, up from 287,767 four days earlier; Ta'iz remains the largest governorate (45%), followed by Lahj (24%) and Aden (19%).

WHO delivered trauma and emergency-surgery kits to hospitals in Taiz city, which remains almost entirely surrounded by Houthi forces, amid acute shortages of medicines, fuel and water; in Marib, WHO said primary healthcare is nearing collapse from funding cuts, with just 6 of 31 mobile medical teams still operating and 15 health facilities shut.

WHO's Situation Report #9 (20-25 October) recorded cumulative casualties rising to 9,072 (7,395 injured, 1,677 deaths), up 559 in six days; Marib emerged as the most lethal front (45 deaths among 143 casualties), and Shabwah's Al-Alam Camp missile-strike toll was revised upward to 235 casualties (69 deaths).

IOM's DTM update dataset (25 October) recorded displacement since the escalation began in June 2026 rising to 276,301 people (46,044 households) as of 24 October, up from 259,807 a week earlier; Ta'iz remains the largest governorate (46%), followed by Lahj (25%) and Aden (17%).

IOM's DTM Update #15 (21 October) recorded displacement since the escalation began in June 2026 rising to 259,807 people (43,295 households), up from 256,591 a week earlier, after a further 8,682 people were displaced on 20 October alone; Ta'iz remains the largest origin/destination governorate (48%).

WHO's Situation Report #8 (12-19 October) recorded cumulative casualties rising to 8,513 (1,574 deaths, 6,939 injured), up 1,340 in eight days as fighting opened a new front in Shabwah (216 casualties, 51 deaths in two days); IOM recorded displacement up 28% to 256,591 since 7 October, and Taiz city's hospital system neared breaking point with its main supply road cut.

IOM's DTM Update #14 (1 Aug-13 Oct) puts Yemen displacement at 227,683, up from ~200,000 in early October; Ta'iz accounts for 53% of the total, followed by Lahj (23%) and Aden (12%). The Houthis have largely encircled Taiz, cutting most remaining supply routes from government-held areas as prices surge.

The Houthis tightened their siege of Taiz at the start of October, seizing its last main road to government-held areas. WHO's cholera toll rose to 8,034 cases (27 deaths) and measles to 22,800+ cases (128 deaths) this year; its 90-day response is only 14% funded ($4.3M of $31M). Saudi Arabia said a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's airport killed 12, wounded 300+.

UNHCR's Yemen Situation External Update #2 recorded a separate, more precise displacement count: about 142,000 people newly displaced across seven governorates between 1 August and 27 September, mostly sheltering in Taiz, Lahj and Aden; its 2026 funding appeal remains only 18% funded.

UN News reported that Yemeni health authorities' toll rose to 959 deaths and 4,207 injuries across 10 governorates as of 2 October; IOM put displacement above 200,000 (close to 3,800 in Djibouti) and WHO counted nearly 198,000 uprooted, with less than 1% having received health services. WHO's funding requirement rose from $9 million to $31 million, plus $700,000 more for Djibouti refugees.

UN News reported, citing WHO and Aden health authorities, that cumulative casualties since 6 August have risen to more than 4,481 (830 deaths), still climbing by roughly 100 per day; displacement inside Yemen has risen past 180,000, and only about 60% of health facilities remain fully functional amid nine damaged, out-of-service or attacked facilities near Taiz, Lahj and Hudaydah.

UN News reported, citing WHO/Aden health authorities and UNICEF, a deepening health and child crisis alongside the conflict: ~7,800 suspected cholera cases (22 deaths), 22,000+ measles cases and dengue linked to 37 deaths; UNICEF verified 15 children killed and 14 injured since 3 September among ~71,000 displaced children, with over a quarter of 2,900 screened acutely malnourished.

The UN Security Council condemned continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia affecting civilian and energy infrastructure in a press statement issued 18 September, demanding an immediate end to the military escalation; UNHCR reported displacement inside Yemen has risen past 130,000 since the start of September, with Djibouti arrivals projected to exceed 10,000 by mid-October.

OCHA Djibouti's Flash Update No. 1 (15 Sept) put Djibouti crossings at 2,500+ as of 14 Sept, since risen to 3,000+ per UN News; WHO's SitRep #3 confirmed 2,883 cumulative casualties (504 deaths, 2,379 injuries) as of 12 Sept and DFA control of the west coast except Midi district.

IOM reported on 18 September that displacement inside Yemen has reached at least 112,000 people over two weeks of fighting (up from 93,864 as of 15 September), mainly along the west coast and in Aden, Hudaydah, Abyan and Taiz; more than 3,000 people (up from 2,400) have now crossed to Djibouti, and IOM warned its relief stocks will soon be depleted.

The Security Council held an emergency session on Yemen as WHO's cumulative casualty count since 6 August rose to 2,883 and IOM separately recorded 93,864 people newly displaced this month; UNHCR reported over 2,400 people have fled to Djibouti within four days, and the UN released $9 million from CERF for the displaced.

OCHA reported hostilities since 1 September have displaced at least 125,000 people (18,000 households) in Yemen, with 80,000 displaced in recent days alone; OHCHR verified 40 civilian casualties (8 killed, 32 injured) between 1-14 September. Houthi forces seized further Red Sea islands beyond Mocha, tightening control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
WHO reported 67 deaths and 288 injuries across seven Yemeni governorates between 6-24 August 2026, per UN News -- the most comprehensive casualty count yet published for the current escalation.

IOM reported at least 46,000 people displaced by fighting across Yemen's West Coast and Taiz governorates since 3 September, with OCHA documenting at least 14 civilians killed or wounded since the start of the month; pro-government forces reportedly withdrew from an island base in the Bab al-Mandab Strait on 11 September, a day after Houthi forces captured the Red Sea port of Mocha.

Houthi forces captured the Red Sea port of Mocha and seized eight UN vehicles on 10 September; UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council Yemen's 2022 truce has collapsed into 'a new, more dangerous phase of war,' with more than 11,400 households newly displaced since 3 September across five governorates.
